overlap_rationale: Study A (Gopakumar 2014, IJURR) and Study B (Gopakumar 2012, Routledge monograph) share nested qualitative dissertation fieldwork on the Bengaluru (Koramangala slum cluster) water-supply partnership, whereas Study B additionally covers Chennai and Kochi. Specifically, Study A acknowledges NSF Dissertation Improvement Grant SES-0620894 (alongside a 2011 FRQSC write-up grant), cites semi-structured interviews and a focus group conducted in June–July 2006, and examines the 2004 BWSSB–SDU–NGO–slum partnership in Bengaluru's Koramangala slum cluster involving BWSSB Assistant Engineers (AE), the Social Development Unit (SDU), the Koramangala Slum Development Committee, WATSAN committees, and the Karnataka Slum Dwellers Federation (KKNSS), while citing Gopakumar (2012). Study B explicitly states in its Acknowledgments that the book began as Gopakumar's PhD dissertation at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, outlines in Chapter 1 a comparative investigation of national-to-state policy transmission (Chapter 3), urban water supply regimes in Bengaluru, Chennai, and Kochi (Chapter 4), and three water supply partnership cases—one each in Bengaluru, Chennai, and Kochi (Chapter 5)—and lists in its Abbreviations the exact Bengaluru Koramangala case organizations from Study A (BWSSB, AE, SDU, KSDC [Koramangala Slum Development Committee], KKNSS, WATSAN, NBR [Natkal Balancing Reservoir], and NTU [new trade union]). Thus, Study A re-theorizes the Bengaluru partnership component of the multi-city dissertation fieldwork using an STS 'urban laboratory' and 'archipelagos/tendrils' framework, creating partial sample overlap on the Bengaluru case. Confidence is rated medium rather than high because the retrieved 34-page PDF for Study B contains only the front matter, Chapter 1 (pp. 1–6), and References (pp. 142–152), omitting Chapters 2–6 (pp. 7–141), so exact interview sample sizes in Table 2.1 and direct quote-by-quote overlap in Chapter 5 cannot be inspected verbatim.
study_a_sample_and_data: Single-city qualitative case study of a pilot urban water-supply partnership launched in 2004 in the Koramangala slum cluster (LR Nagara, Shastri Nagara, Ambedkar Nagara, and Rajendra Nagara) in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India, involving the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB), its Social Development Unit (SDU), participating NGOs, Koramangala Slum Development Committee, WATSAN committees, and Karnataka Slum Dwellers Federation (KKNSS). Supported by NSF Dissertation Improvement Grant No. SES-0620894 and FRQSC Grant 2011-NP-140665. Empirical data comprise in-depth semi-structured interviews and a focus group conducted in June–July 2006 (exact total N not reported; footnotes cite junior BWSSB Assistant Engineers ENG1 and ENG2, NGO staff NGO1–NGO3, a WATSAN committee member, and a 29 July 2006 slum resident focus group).
study_b_sample_and_data: Comparative qualitative monograph derived from the author's PhD dissertation at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute examining water supply reform policy transmission across three Indian states (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala), urban water supply regimes, and three public–private water supply partnership cases—one each in Bengaluru (Bangalore), Chennai, and Kochi. Note on text completeness: the retrieved 34-page PDF contains front matter, Contents, List of Illustrations, Preface, Acknowledgments, Abbreviations, Chapter 1 (pp. 1–6), and References (pp. 142–152), but omits Chapters 2–6 (pp. 7–141). Consequently, exact interview counts and dates in Table 2.1 ('Details of interviews conducted at research sites', p. 12) and the empirical text of Chapter 5 (pp. 82–117) cannot be verified directly, although the Abbreviations list confirms inclusion of the exact Bengaluru Koramangala partnership actors (BWSSB, SDU, KSDC, KKNSS, WATSAN) alongside Chennai (CMWSSB, TWAD Board) and Kochi (KWA, VKSS, VWSC) cases.
